test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following Five-Year Plans marked a strategic transition in India's economic policy, shifting the primary focus from agriculture to the development of heavy industries and industrialization?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Second Five-Year Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) marked a **strategic shift in India's economic policy**, emphasizing the development of heavy industries and industrialization over agriculture.
 
• This plan was based on the **Mahalnobis Model**, which prioritized industrialization and aimed at building the foundation of a self-reliant economy by focusing on sectors like steel, machinery, and infrastructure.
 
• Under the plan, **heavy industries** such as steel plants in Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela were established with assistance from countries like the Soviet Union, the UK, and Germany.
 
• The plan also aimed at achieving **economic self-sufficiency** and reducing dependence on foreign imports by strengthening industries that could produce capital goods and machinery.
 
• This strategic transition was driven by the vision of India becoming a **socialist economy**, with the state playing a dominant role in major industries, while agriculture was considered a secondary priority during this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956):**

 
 
• The focus was primarily on **agriculture**, irrigation, and land reforms to address food shortages and support rural development.
 
• It emphasized **community development programs** and prioritized the agricultural sector to stabilize the newly independent economy.
 
• The plan achieved significant success in boosting **agricultural production** and laid the foundation for future economic planning.
 
 
 
• **Third Five-Year Plan (1961-1966):**
 
 
• The primary goal was to establish a **self-reliant economy** with an emphasis on agriculture and industry.
 
• However, this plan faced challenges due to the **Indo-China War (1962)**, the **Indo-Pak War (1965)**, and severe droughts, which diverted resources away from planned objectives.
 
• Despite setbacks, it contributed to the development of industries and infrastructure in India.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-1974):**
 
 
• Focusing on **growth with stability** and reducing income inequality, this plan sought to address the disparities in economic development.
 
• It emphasized the **Green Revolution**, which transformed Indian agriculture through the introduction of high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation infrastructure.
 
• The plan's success in agriculture helped India achieve food self-sufficiency.
 
 
 
• **Fifth Five-Year Plan (1974-1979):**
 
 
• This plan emphasized **poverty alleviation** and self-reliance, introducing programs like the **Minimum Needs Program** and the **Twenty-Point Program**.
 
• It also focused on achieving **economic growth** while addressing the basic needs of the population, such as food, housing, and healthcare.
 
 
 
• **Mahalnobis Model:**
 
 
• Introduced by **Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**, this economic model formed the basis of the Second Five-Year Plan.
 
• The model emphasized the importance of **capital goods industries** to create a self-reliant economy and reduce dependence on foreign imports.
 
• It highlighted the role of the public sector in driving industrial growth and laid the foundation for India's mixed economy.
